Hi guys i'm new in these forums and holography so please be patient and kindly forgive the many questions.

So, starting from the beginning, i have been interested in holography for about ten years but never actually took the plunge in making my own due to the monetary factor ( i was 15 at the time ) but i did buy some books and a few holograms.

Now that i have a steady income and some extra cash i became re-interested in holography, making my own holograms in particular.

My basic aim is to open a small holographic art gallery or exhibition in Malta to intruduce and create interest of this wonderful art in my small country since as far as i know holography is unknown here ( apart from the ones on Visas ).

Now, i believe that 2.5" x 2.5" or 4" x 5" holograms are not going to be big enough to create the desired impact. I believe that at least an 8" x 10" or 11" x 14" size is required for that wow effect that will be remembered.

I am therefore thinking of setting up a small lab to produce good quality 8" x 10" and 11" x 14" transmittion masters and image plane reflection copies ( .

According to what i have learned so far the best setup woud be a split beam with a collimated reference beam and two object beams. i am therefore going to need the following ( please correct me if i'm wrong ):

High power laser

Laser shutter

Front surface mirrors

Bi-concave lenses

Collimating mirror

Spatial Filter

Variable beam splitter

50/50 beam splitter

Plate holder

Light meter

Optical bench

Recording film / plates

Developing and processing chemicals

The laser: He-Ne or DPSS ? red or green ? 100mW powerful enough ? 

I have been looking around and noted that gas lasers with high powers are pretty expensive ( at least too expensive for me ) so i guess it leaves me with the DPSS option. although there seems to be some fear of DPSS due to mode hopping i have seen that some ppl on these forums use the Coherent Compass 315M ( too expensive new but maybe used ), how good is it for holography ? is it good enough and powerful enough for my application ? are there other 100mW ( or more ) DPSS lasers ( possibly cheaper ) that are good for my application ? i also saw somewhere that something called an ETALON is used to stop mode hopping but i cannot figure out what it is exactly as the descriptions are a bit complicated.

also what is TTL and is it needed ? is it good or bad for holography ?

Laser shutter: are there any ones which are recomended ?

Front surface mirrors: not much to say here

Bi-concave lenses: what size and focal length. are there any types that are better than others.

Collimating mirror: i have found 13.1" f4.5 collimating mirror at a not too expensive price found here [http://www.murni.com/mirrors1.htm](http://www.murni.com/mirrors1.htm) will this size be big enough for 11" x 14" ?

Spatial filter: what size objective and pinhole ? any good value for money ones ?

Variable beam splitter: where from ?

50/50 beam splitter: with or without polarizer/filter etc.. ?

Plate holder: i can make this one.

Light meter: any cheap ones ?

Optical bench: i can build this one wth limestone slabs.

Recording film / plates: There are many types/brands to choose from here and Slavich/Colourholographics films/plates and homemade DCG seem to be the most popular. 

making my own DCG is too time consuming and complicated for me so ill stick to ready made ones. i have also seen the polygrama photopolymer which seems interesting as it needs no chemicals to develop.

So from your experience which would be the best suited for 8"x 10" and 11" x 14" sizes with reference to brightness, image quality, exposure times, ease of use, and finally price.

I am leaning towads the polygrama photopolymer due to the ease of use and elimination of chemicals to process but it seems a bit expensive. how many milliliters would be needed to coat an 8" x 10" or 11" x 14" plate ? also i have read somewhere that it needs a lot of energy to expose, what would be a typical exposure time for an 8" x 10" plate with a 100mW laser ? Also, can the replay color be changed in the same way as film with TEA ?

Developing and processing chemicals: i guess the ones suggested by the manufacturer of the chosen films/plates.

And finally where do i buy all of this stuff at reasonable prices that will ship overseas.

Your comments / answers for the above as well as any help will be greatly appreciated.

Thanking you in advance and apologizing for the many, many questions.

Mike

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
You will not need to learn about Etalons yet. They go inside the laser cavity and unless you start redesigning your laser don't worry to much about them.

I would choose green right now. It is the best deal in lasers.

I am working on a post on figuring out focal lengths. Tom B. sent me some good information, I just need to find some time to write it up. 

For the powers we are talking about a variable mirror beam splitter is fine.

A 13.1 inch mirror is a little too small. See wler's site for some interesting math.

The set up you are describing is what it has taken me 5 years to aquire. I have been able to make holograms the whole time by settling for less. While you design your perfect bench, get an Integraf kit and make some holograms! You will learn stuff about handling the materials and it's fun.

> **Amonra:** Ok but does the 315M need an ETALON ?

No, the C315 is a ring laser and it gets it's coherence length with another principle.

> **Amonra:** I would prefer green too but from a recording media / supplies point, there seems to be much more for the RED than there is for the green. also most emulsions seem to be more sensitive to the red than they are to the green.

You have all the options as far as grain size for green but you might have to settle for pan chromatic sensitivity. This is not a problem but makes safe-lighting a little more complicated.

> **Amonra:** I also guess that red ones are cheaper or have more power for the same price but i was so far unable to find suitable high power red diode lasers, do you know of any ? it would be nice to have both options to compare before i decide.

I have used the Analog Technologies laser and I like it. I never had it mode hop but Kris reports it will once and a while. It was running about $800 last I checked. They had delivery problems in the past but that is all resolved now.

> **Amonra:** I have seen in some post here that there were some cheap variable mirror wheels from a surplus store but they were a bit thin. someone had to test adding another glass but i cannot find that post now to see how it went.

I have one and I can make it work (I don't need it yet). Thicker glass would be nice. Having a few variable beam splitters around is a good thing and you will always find a way to make one work. The first beam splitter has to be very easy to use. The rest you can play with.

> **Amonra:** I'm not familiar with wler's site do you have an address.

[http://perso.orange.fr/redlum.xohp/argonlaser.html](http://perso.orange.fr/redlum.xohp/argonlaser.html)

It is really your choice. We have not tested both designs. I like anamorphic prism pairs but the spec on the circularized diodes look good.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
Actually, the C315 is not a ring laser. The way it gets it's great coherence length is through strict control of the temperature of the KTP crystal. In the C315, the KTP has a dual function. It acts as a frequency doubler, and also as a etalon. Because the temperature range at which the KTP doubles the frequency efficiently is rather broad, that left the engineers room to use the same crystal as an etalon by fine tuning it's temperature (and thus it's thickness) to ensure single line operation. The following link describes this: [http://members.misty.com/don/laserssl.htm#sslc315f](http://members.misty.com/don/laserssl.htm#sslc315f).

Coherent does sell a ring YAG laser. It is called the Coherent Compass 532 laser.
